newsitem.title: FRANCE: SGS-Thomson falls by over 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: SGS-Thomson falls by over 10 pct.

text.p: Shares in semiconductor group SGS-Thomson Microelectronics were over 10 percent down in afternoon trade on the Paris bourse, and down by more on Wall Street, following the company's 1996 earnings reports and a warning for the first quarter.
In Paris, SGS-Thomson was down 10.21 percent at 387 francs at 1402 GMT while in New York it was down nine dollars to 70-1/4.
It had hit a low of 380.20 in Paris.
"There is an awful lot of profit-taking. Now that it is falling 12 percent people are seeing a disaster, but it has been rising a lot in January," said a dealer.
"It seems UBS has downgraded to a "neutral" and other analysts may follow but it remains a good stock," he added.
SGS-Thomson rose from 361 francs on January 2 -- and from a low of 154.50 on July 16 -- to 433 franc on January 20.
